page: Amazon Web Services m5n.4xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, delivering 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache alongside support for Advanced Vector Extensions, including AVX-512. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is positioned in the bottom 25% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests. Conversely, multi-core performance rises to the middle 50% tier in stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core evaluations. Memory bandwidth, including both cached small block reads at 754.06 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 89.11 GB/sec, consistently registers in the average tier.

Network baseline bandwidth is rated at 16 Gbps, supporting network-intensive tasks. The instance demonstrates average performance for Redis SET operations, static web serving, and small-model LLM inference. Qualitatively, the m5n.4xlarge offers balanced resource density for general-purpose enterprise workloads, though its lower single-core efficiency suggests it is less suited for single-threaded tasks. It is best utilized for multi-threaded applications, web serving, database operations, and general-purpose workloads requiring stable network throughput.
